info.title: GetGPX API
info.description:
## Getting started

GetGPX API v1 exposes public track data and authenticated track management on the same origin as the website. This reference documents **all** supported track operations. Metadata and geometry are deliberately separate.

```sh
curl -H 'Accept: application/json' 'https://getgpx.com/api/v1/tracks/TRACK_ID'
curl 'https://getgpx.com/api/v1/tracks/TRACK_ID/analysis'
curl -OJ 'https://getgpx.com/api/v1/tracks/TRACK_ID/gpx'
```

Replace the example host with your GetGPX deployment and TRACK_ID with the public ID from a track URL.

## Authentication today

The three public GET operations need no login. All other operations require the existing **HttpOnly getgpx_session cookie**. Sign in on the website first, then return to this documentation on the same origin. The browser supplies its cookie automatically; Swagger cannot create an HttpOnly cookie using its Authorize dialog. Never paste a session cookie into documentation or browser storage. Scripts can use an existing cookie jar (`curl --cookie session.cookies ...`); this is an interim mechanism, not a supported automated login flow. Sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity and renew on activity. There are no API keys, personal tokens, API OAuth flow, or mandatory User-Agent requirements yet.

Google sign-in (/auth/*), the homepage feed (/homepage), health checks and internal signing routes are website/infrastructure features, not this API contract.

## Upload and processing

Send raw GPX with Content-Type: application/gpx+xml, a percent-encoded X-GPX-Filename and X-Track-Type. A successful upload returns 202 and Location. Poll that status URL with your session until READY or FAILED. Keep any active result visible during replacement. Mutation examples are executable and can permanently change or delete your own data.

## Data conventions

Distances use km, elevations m, speeds km/h, durations ms and slopes/percentages percent. Dates use UTC ISO 8601. Missing data is null or absent as the schema specifies. The author is the uploader. Titles and filenames are user content. Public IDs are opaque and case-sensitive. Lists contain at most 24 items with an opaque nextCursor. Success JSON uses data, except the standalone analysis document; GPX is a file. Error codes are stable; human-readable messages are optional and must not be parsed.

## Browser access and compatibility

Same-origin browser requests and direct server/CLI calls are supported. Cross-origin browser scripts are refused; no CORS access is granted. This is not a restriction on server-side proxies. Public download links and safe top-level navigation remain possible. POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE always enforce the existing session/ownership rules.

v1 is a stable contract. Clients should ignore unfamiliar additive fields and tolerate new category IDs. Incompatible changes require a new major version and a migration plan. The application release number is independent of API version. Rate limits/User-Agent policies and personal tokens are later phases.

post.description: Requires a website session. Source is stored durably before 202; processing continues asynchronously. Poll the Location URL. User tier quota applies (BASIC: 100, PREMIUM: 1,000 by default).

Location.description: Relative URL of the owner-only processing status endpoint.
